key_insight: A few design choices — especially action grounding, instruction-aligned supervision, and diverse task/data coverage — matter more than raw model scale for building useful vision–language–action (VLA) models for generalist robots. Systematic comparisons show which components most strongly drive real-world robot performance.
problem_solved: Clarifies which architectural, data and training choices actually improve VLA model usefulness for embodied control, resolving uncertainty about whether scale, objectives, or data diversity are the primary drivers of robot generalization.
method: Systematic comparison of multiple VLA model variants across key axes: data composition, training objectives (language-aligned vs task-only), action representations, and model modularity.
Controlled ablation studies and benchmark evaluations spanning simulated tasks and real-world robot experiments to measure transfer and robustness.
Derive practical guidelines from empirical results to prioritize design choices for deploying generalist robotic agents.
impact: Provides actionable guidance for ML and robotics practitioners on where to invest effort (e.g., grounded action representations and aligned instruction data) to improve robot generalization and reduce wasted compute on unhelpful scaling. Accelerates development of reliable, generalist robot behaviors by focusing on the most effective components.
visual_elements: Importance heatmap: factors (data diversity, instruction alignment, action grounding, model scale) vs. performance to show relative impact.
Pipeline schematic: perception → language grounding → action representation → controller, highlighting recommended design choices at each stage.
Ablation bar chart: performance drop when removing each key component (e.g., no instruction tuning, ungrounded actions).
Real-world vs. simulation side‑by‑side: short sequence of robot tasks showing transfer differences under different model designs.
paper_title: What matters in building vision–language–action models for generalist robots
paper_authors: Xinghang Li, Peiyan Li, Long Qian, Minghuan Liu, Dong Wang
